name: Uzzi
overview: Uzzi was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Michri. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his lineage, without additional notes or narrative detail. This establishes him as a distinct individual within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzzi means 'y-h-v-h is [my] strength,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that acknowledges the Lord as the source of strength. This proper name, not given directly by God, highlights the believer's reliance on divine power as understood in the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uzzi as the son of Michri. Additionally, it is inferred that Elah was his father, situating Uzzi within a family line in the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Uzzi's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8. This situates him among the faithful remnant of Israel, preserving the heritage and continuity of God's people. Though not a prominent figure in biblical narrative events, his inclusion underscores the importance of lineage and God's providential care through generations.
